title: Horizontal Stabiliser Box Lower Skin — Corrosion Blend-Out and Doubler Repair
abstract: Blend-out of corrosion on the horizontal stabiliser box lower skin and, beyond the blend limit, installation of an external doubler with the fastener pattern and inspection interval it carries.

sections.purpose: This repair removes corrosion from the horizontal stabiliser box lower skin by blending, and where the resulting material loss exceeds the blend limit, restores the section with an external doubler.
sections.damage_assessment: Corrosion on this surface is almost always at a fastener row and almost always started at a disbonded sealant fillet, so look along the whole row rather than at the one place the paint has blistered. Measure the remaining thickness by ultrasonic gauge on a grid at twenty-five millimetre spacing across the affected area, and take four extra readings around any point that is below nominal. Record the grid, not a single minimum. Where the loss is at a shear tie D5510114141932 or at a fitting D5510114182451, the doubler route is not available and the item must be assessed by engineering, because the load path is local rather than in the skin.
sections.repair_procedure: 1. Clean the area and remove the protective scheme locally. 2. Measure the remaining thickness on the grid and record every reading. 3. Where the loss is inside the blend limit, blend it out to a smooth radius of not less than twenty times the depth removed, working along the grain. 4. Re-measure the blended area and confirm it is inside the limit. 5. Restore the protective scheme in accordance with the applicable scheme. 6. Where the loss exceeds the blend limit, do not blend further. Prepare the area for the doubler. 7. Drill the doubler pattern with the jig, working from the centre outwards, and de-burr every hole. 8. Do an eddy current inspection of every drilled hole. 9. Install the doubler using the stiffener D5510119125169 as a backing where the drawing calls for it, with the shear ties D5510114141932 at each end. 10. Install the fasteners wet with sealant, and torque them in the marked sequence. 11. Fit the grommet AGS825520K1 where the harness passes the doubler edge. 12. Seal the doubler edge all round with a fillet. 13. Restore the protective scheme over the whole repair.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection of every fastener hole in the doubler pattern at installation and record the results. Repeat the eddy current inspection of the doubler perimeter row every four thousand flight cycles. Do a detailed visual inspection of the sealant fillet at every heavy check; a fillet that has lifted is the mechanism that put the corrosion there in the first place and it will do it again under the doubler where nothing can be seen.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Blend-out up to 15 per cent of nominal skin thickness over an area not exceeding 10 000 square millimetres, not closer than 20 mm to a fastener row. Beyond that, the doubler repair applies up to 25 per cent loss.

repair_drawings.title: External doubler and fastener pattern, stabiliser box lower skin

materials.description: SHEAR TIE, STABILIZER BOX STRUCTURE, SUB-ASSY

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows, 20 mm pitch, 15 mm edge distance, staggered; fasteners installed wet with sealant
type_data.fatigue_life_note: The doubler repair is life-limited to 20 000 flight cycles with a repeat eddy current inspection of the perimeter row every 4 000 flight cycles. A blend-out inside the blend limit carries no life limit.
